answers.question: I'm new to the OpenMRS O3 codebase. What does the billing feature consist of, and which repositories implement it?

paragraphs.text: Billing in OpenMRS O3 is made of **two repositories working together**, plus documentation. The user-facing feature is a frontend microfrontend (a separately built JavaScript module that plugs into the O3 SPA), and it needs a Java backend module for storage, business rules and the REST API. Nothing in the O3 docs bundles them into one install; you install the backend module on the server and the frontend module into the SPA.
## The two repositories that implement it

| Repository | Role | Language |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openmrs-module-billing` | Backend: data model, services, REST API, FHIR `Invoice` | Java (Maven, multi-module: `api`, `omod`, `fhir`) |
| `openmrs-esm-billing-app` | Frontend: the screens and forms a cashier or clerk uses | TypeScript / React |

The docs describe exactly this split: the frontend "depends on the OpenMRS Billing backend module to function properly" [1]. The frontend declares that dependency mechanically in its route manifest, requiring backend module `billing` version `>=2.5.0-0` and `webservices.rest >=2.24.0` [2].
## What the feature does
The backend README is the clearest inventory of the functionality [3]. In plain terms:

- **Bills and line items** — a `Bill` is "a list of `BillLineItem`s and `Payment`s created by a cashier for a patient" [4]. It records the cashier (`Provider`), the patient, the `CashPoint` (the physical cashier station), the `Visit`, and a `receiptNumber` [5].
- **Payments** — multiple payment modes, partial payments, change calculation, cashier attribution.
- **Receipts** — printable receipts with sequential or custom numbering.
- **Billable services and pricing** — the catalogue of chargeable services and their prices, including price history.
- **Discounts and refunds** — both with an audit trail and an approval flow; a bill's net amount subtracts approved, non-voided discounts, and the code deliberately keeps `voided` rows out of the "active" views so the audit history stays intact [6].
- **Exemptions** — rules, written in JavaScript, that make an ordered service non-chargeable, evaluated against patient age and order details.
- **Cashier timesheets, financial reports, and automatic bill generation from clinical orders.**
## How the frontend is organised

The frontend is a React app registered through the O3 extension system, not a standalone site. Its routes are declared in a manifest: one standalone page (`billable-services`) plus a set of extensions that attach to slots owned by other modules [7]. That is why billing appears *inside* the patient chart, the visit summary and the homepage dashboard rather than only at its own URL.
The slots it hangs off are worth knowing:

- `homepage-dashboard-slot` for the Billing dashboard tile [8]
- `patient-chart-dashboard-slot` and `patient-chart-billing-dashboard-slot` for the patient's billing history tab [9]
- `visit-summary-panels` for a "Bills" panel on the visit [10]
- `extra-visit-attribute-slot` for a billing payment section in the check-in form [11]
- `patient-banner-tags-slot` for payment-status and visit-attribute tags at the top of the chart [12]

Those component names are wired to real code in the module's entry point `src/index.ts`, which exports each one with `getSyncLifecycle` or `getAsyncLifecycle` so the SPA can load it lazily [13]. The module also ships three workspaces (side panels) and thirteen modals — create/edit bill items, finalize a bill, request a discount, review refunds and so on [14].

Within `src/`, the folders map almost one-to-one onto the backend features: `billing-dashboard`, `invoice`, `bills-table`, `bill-history`, `billable-services`, `discounts`, `refunds`, `payment-status-tag`, `visit-bills`, `billing-form`.
## How the two halves talk to each other

The frontend never touches the database; it calls the backend's REST API. All of that traffic is funnelled through one module, `src/billing.resource.ts` [15], which builds URLs and wraps them in SWR hooks (SWR is the data-fetching/caching library). For example `usePaginatedBills` requests `/bill` with a custom representation listing only the fields the table needs, and passes paging, status, patient-name and date filters as query parameters [16]. Note the comment explaining that the backend rejects an inverted date range with HTTP 400, so the hook deliberately skips the request instead [17].

A second layer transforms the raw API shape into something the UI likes: `mapBillProperties` parses the patient's `display` string into identifier and name, sums the tendered payments, and renames `total` to `totalAmount` and `amountAfterDiscount` to `netAmount` [18].

On the backend those URLs are served by classes in the `omod` module under `web/rest/resource`, one per entity — `BillResource`, `PaymentResource`, `BillLineItemResource`, `CashPointResource`, `TimesheetResource`, `BillDiscountResource`, `BillRefundResource`, `BillableServiceResource`, `BillExemptionResource` and others [19]. They sit on top of service interfaces in the `api` module such as `BillService`, `BillLineItemService`, `PaymentModeService`, `CashPointService` and `ItemPriceService`, whose implementations live in `api/impl`.
## The FHIR side

There is a third piece inside the same backend repository: the `fhir` Maven submodule, which exposes bills as FHIR `Invoice` resources. `InvoiceFhirResourceProvider` is annotated `@R4Provider` and implements the HAPI `IResourceProvider` contract, delegating reads to `FhirInvoiceService` and translating the internal model with `InvoiceTranslatorImpl` [20]. It is built "against the `fhir2` module" [21], which is why `openmrs-module-fhir2` is a required module [22].
## The other repositories you selected
Three of the six repositories you picked do not contain billing code, and I checked rather than assumed:

- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs` — the documentation. It only describes the feature [1] and mentions the billing app among the modules migrated to rspack/Vitest for testing.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-management` and `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib` — no matches at all for "billing" or "Invoice" in their TypeScript/TSX/JSON files. They are the *hosts*: patient-management owns the patient chart and visit summary slots that billing's extensions attach to, and form-engine-lib renders the forms; neither contains billing logic.
- `openmrs-module-fhir2` — the only match is a list of FHIR resource type names in `FhirUtils` that happens to include the word `Invoice` [23]. The billing module supplies the actual `Invoice` provider; fhir2 provides the hosting framework.
## What I did not verify

I read the frontend's structure, resource layer, route manifest and entry point, and the backend's package layout, `Bill` model, REST resource names and FHIR provider, plus the README and the O3 docs page. I did not open the service implementations, the controllers' request mappings, the cashier/timesheet/report code in detail, or the frontend's individual components — so the feature list above is taken from the module README and file layout rather than traced line by line. I also could not list every module dependency (for instance `event` and `idgen`, mentioned only in the README).

The [Billing app](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-billing-app) is a frontend module designed to streamline financial operations within healthcare settings. It facilitates the management of patient billing, payments, and service pricing. The module integrates with the OpenMRS platform and allows healthcare providers to generate bills, track payments, manage billable services, and handle various financial transactions. It depends on the [OpenMRS Billing backend module](https://github.com/op

The OpenMRS Billing Module is a comprehensive billing and payment management system for OpenMRS. It provides a complete solution for healthcare facilities to manage patient billing, process payments, generate receipts, and track financial transactions.

Create and manage patient bills with multiple line items, track bills and individual line items through their lifecycle (pending, paid, exempted, refunded, etc.), and associate bills with patient visits. Supports bill adjustments with full audit trail.

Apply line-item or whole-bill discounts with a full audit trail. Discounts can be filtered on, and are linked back to the bill so they are purged along with it. Enabled by default; toggle via `billing.discountEnabled`.

Request and approve refunds against paid bills with proper privilege controls. Refunds are surfaced in the bill representation and can be filtered on via the `refundStatus` parameter on `GET /bill`. Enabled by default; toggle via `billing.refundEnabled`.

Resolve a patient's overall payment status (paid / pending / exempted / no active bills) via a pluggable resolver, configurable through the `billing.patientPaymentStatusResolver` global property. Designed to surface payment state without blocking access to clinical forms.

Process payments using multiple payment modes (cash, insurance, mobile money, credit/debit cards, custom modes) with support for partial payments, payment attributes, automatic change calculation, and per-payment cashier attribution.
Generate and print receipts using configurable Jasper Report templates with sequential or custom receipt numbering, configurable logos, and reprint capabilities with privilege controls.
Manage multiple cashier stations/locations with cash point assignment for cashiers and location-based transaction tracking.
Track cashier shifts with clock in/out functionality, configurable timesheet validation for bill creation, auto-close timesheets, and shift-based reporting.
Manage billable healthcare services, configure item prices with price history tracking, and integrate with OpenMRS Stock Management module.

Exempt a service or commodity from billing when an order for it is placed. Each exemption targets a concept and carries one or more JavaScript rules, evaluated against the patient's age (`patientAge`) and basic order details (`order.uuid`, `order.conceptId`), so age-based and order-based criteria are supported.
Generate shift summary reports, daily shift summaries, department collections, department revenue, and payments by payment mode reports.
Automatically generate billable items and bill line items from clinical orders, including medication orders, with order-to-bill line item mapping.

Provides REST API endpoints at `/rest/v1/billing/*` for bills, payments, payment modes, billable services, cash points, item prices, discounts, refunds, and patient payment status. Includes patient dashboard integration for OpenMRS 2.x with configurable bill history widget. Supports English, French, and Spanish translations.
Exposes bills as FHIR `Invoice` resources via the `fhir` submodule, built against the `fhir2` module. Supports OpenMRS Platform 2.5, 2.6, and 2.7 FHIR variants.
